content:
The [Currency Converter](/currency-converter) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Convert money between world currencies at live exchange rates. Enter your amount, from currency and to currency and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A currency converter turns an amount in one currency into another at the current exchange rate. Rates are fetched live from a free exchange-rate service when you open the page, cached for an hour, and shown with the date they were published. If the rate service is unreachable, the converter says so clearly instead of showing a stale or invented figure. Rates move through the day, and banks and card providers add their own margin on top — so use the result as a guide for travel, shopping and budgeting, and check the rate your provider will actually apply before sending money.

## How to use the Currency Converter

Start by entering your amount, then choosing your from currency from the list and finally choosing your to currency from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter the amount of money you want to convert.
2. Choose the currency it is in, then the currency you want to convert to.
3. Check the converted amount and the exchange rate used, plus the date the rate was published.
4. Try different amounts — the conversion updates instantly.

## Formula

Converted amount = amount × (rate of target currency ÷ rate of source currency), where both rates are quoted against the US dollar. The rates are mid-market rates — the midpoint between buy and sell prices.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Currency Converter](/currency-converter) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Converting $100 to euros at a rate of 0.92 EUR per USD gives €92. The same $100 at a rate of 0.85 GBP per USD gives £85. The exact figures change with the live rate shown on the page. Try the same figures in the [Currency Converter](/currency-converter) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Currency Converter](/currency-converter) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What is the mid-market rate?

The mid-market rate is the midpoint between the buy and sell prices on the foreign-exchange market — the rate banks use with each other. It is the fairest reference rate, but it is not the rate you get as a customer: banks, card networks and money-transfer services add a margin, typically 1–3%, and sometimes a fixed fee. A converter showing the mid-market rate will therefore show slightly more than you actually receive.

## Why rates change

Exchange rates move constantly while markets are open, driven by interest-rate decisions, inflation data, trade flows and political news. A rate that is right in the morning can be different by the afternoon. For large transfers, the timing of the conversion can matter as much as the amount — but predicting short-term moves is not possible, so treat the rate as a snapshot, not a forecast.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Compare the total cost, not just the rate — fees can outweigh a good rate on small amounts.
- Avoid converting at airports and hotels; their margins are usually the worst.
- For travel, a card with no foreign-transaction fee often beats exchanging cash.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are the exchange rates live?

Yes — rates are fetched from a free exchange-rate service when the page loads and are cached for about an hour. The date of the rate is shown on the page, so you can see how fresh it is. Try it with your own numbers in the [Currency Converter](/currency-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why does my bank give me a different amount?

Banks and card providers add a margin to the mid-market rate and sometimes charge a fee. The converter shows the mid-market reference rate, which is the fairest comparison point but not the rate you will actually receive. Try it with your own numbers in the [Currency Converter](/currency-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What happens if the rates cannot be loaded?

The converter shows a clear message instead of a number. Check your connection and try again — it never shows a stale or invented rate as if it were live. Try it with your own numbers in the [Currency Converter](/currency-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Currency Converter use?

Converted amount = amount × (rate of target currency ÷ rate of source currency), where both rates are quoted against the US dollar. The rates are mid-market rates — the midpoint between buy and sell prices. You can see it in action in the [Currency Converter](/currency-converter) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Currency Converter?

Just Amount, From currency and To currency. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
